sm.help._overview.intro: Splatmania adds tools for camera moves, animation, look and export to the splat editor. Here you find a short guide for each tool.
sm.help._overview.title: Splatmania tools
sm.help.aiShots.intro: Suggests ready-made camera moves such as orbit, push-in or crane for an object. You apply a move as a new camera with one click.
sm.help.aiShots.steps:
Open “Camera move suggestions” in the right toolbar.
Click “Use object”: it takes the active box or sphere selection, otherwise the selected splats, otherwise the whole scene.
Frame a nice view and click “Remember angle” (at most 3) so the moves pass through these angles.
Set “Duration (s)” and “Distance” (1 = automatic framing, higher = further away).
To use Claude, click “Settings”, enter your own “API key” in the “AI (Claude)” section, click “Save & test”, then write your “Wish to Claude”.
Click “Suggest camera moves” and look at the previews.
Click “Apply” on a move, or tick several and click “Apply selected”; below you find “Fit timeline length”, “Turn off timeline loop” and “Turn on depth of field”.
sm.help.aiShots.tips:
Without a key or offline, moves are suggested without AI.
With “Use Claude” on, the preview images are sent to Anthropic; costs are billed to your Anthropic account.
Each applied move becomes a new camera and can be undone in one step.
sm.help.aiShots.title: Camera move suggestions
sm.help.align.intro: Lines up several scans of the same scene. You click matching points, then Splatmania aligns everything to the reference.
sm.help.align.steps:
Open the align tool in the right toolbar (J key).
In the panel, use “Reference” to pick the layer that stays fixed.
On the reference, click at least three distinct points that do not lie on a line.
Select the other layer and click the same spots in the same order: point n belongs to point n.
Keep “Include scale” on if the scans differ in size, and click “Align”.
Then click “Refine” for fine alignment; a “Search radius” of 0 means automatic.
sm.help.align.tips:
Drag a point to move it, right-click to delete it; “Clear points” removes all points of the active layer.
The depth filter also hides floaters while you set points.
Existing animation of the layer keeps running relative to its new position.
sm.help.align.title: Align (anchor points)
sm.help.cameras.intro: In the scene manager you create as many shot cameras as you like, animate them with keys and cut them together on the cut track.
sm.help.cameras.steps:
In the scene list, use + next to “Cameras” to add a camera, ⧉ to duplicate the selected one and − to delete it.
Under “View & cut”, pick the “Viewport” mode: “Free”, “Look through” (K key) or “Cut”.
Move to a frame on the timeline, set up the view and press “Add Key” or Enter to key the selected camera.
Drag in an empty area of the cut track to create a shot of the selected camera; drag its edges to trim it, right-click to switch camera or delete it.
With “✎ Edit path (X)” you drag the keys directly in the viewport; Shift-click the path to insert a key.
Under “Selected camera”, choose the “Projection”: “Normal”, “360°” or “360° VR”, and set the “Lens”.
Turn on “Depth of field”, click “Pick focus” and then the surface that should be sharp; “Focus” and “Aperture” can be keyed.
sm.help.cameras.tips:
“Cross-fade” at a cut only applies to video exports with the “Cut” camera; the viewport cuts hard.
Changes that are not keyed are lost when the frame changes: an orange key button shows this.
The camera’s target is its own object: click “Target” under the camera in the scene list, move it with the move tool and key it on its own.
sm.help.cameras.title: Cameras
sm.help.cleanup.intro: Finds floaters, splats outside the main object and invalid splats, and simplifies large layers. It works on the selected layer.
sm.help.cleanup.steps:
Select a splat in the scene list and open “Clean up” in its properties.
Under “Remove floaters”, click “Find floaters”.
Under “Keep cluster”, set the seed on the object with “Seed = pivot” or “Seed = focus” and click “Find outside”.
Under “Invalid splats (NaN)”, click “NaN splats” to find broken splats.
The hits are selected; delete them with Delete, or turn on “Delete directly”.
To simplify, set “Keep %” under “Decimate (new layer)” and click “Run decimate”.
sm.help.cleanup.tips:
Floater and cluster search need a browser with WebGPU.
The defaults are meant for real, metric scans; for small scenes adjust the voxel size and thresholds.
Decimate creates a new layer and only hides the original.
sm.help.cleanup.title: Clean up
sm.help.depthFilter.intro: Limits selection and picking to a depth range in front of the camera. That way you can grab floaters in front of a wall, or the wall behind them.
sm.help.depthFilter.steps:
In the floating “Depth filter” panel, switch on the toggle in the title bar.
Set the distance range from the camera with “Near (m)” and “Far (m)”.
Under “Outside”, choose how splats outside the range appear: “Normal”, “Dim” or “Hide”.
Now select with rectangle, lasso, polygon, brush or click; only splats inside the range are picked.
With “Selection Depth” on in the bottom toolbar (N key), “Min. opacity” sets how opaque a splat must be to be hit.
sm.help.depthFilter.tips:
The filter has no effect on sphere and box selection.
What counts is the centre of a splat; the metres are scene units.
sm.help.depthFilter.title: Depth filter
sm.help.export.intro: Renders your camera moves as a video, a 360° panorama or a stereo 360° for VR headsets, frame by frame at full quality.
sm.help.export.steps:
In the “Render” menu, open “Video” (for stills and panoramas, “Image”).
Under “Camera”, choose “Cut (one MP4)”, a single camera or “All cameras separately”.
Under “Projection”, choose “Standard”, “360° Equirectangular” or “360° Stereo (top/bottom)”.
For stereo, set “Eye distance”, “Pole fade from” and “Stereo quality”.
Set “Resolution”, “Format”, “Frame Rate” and, if wanted, “Motion blur”.
Click “Render” and wait until all frames are done.
sm.help.export.tips:
A camera’s projection from its properties is preselected in the dialog.
Stereo 360° takes much longer; “Draft (48 segments)” is good for a quick test.
“Open in player / VR” in the “Render” menu shows the scene right away in the player with a VR button.
sm.help.export.title: Video, 360° and VR export
sm.help.layerAnim.intro: Animates the opacity, position and display of a single splat layer over time, for example a fade in or out.
sm.help.layerAnim.steps:
Select a splat in the scene list and open “Layer animation” in its properties.
Move to a frame on the timeline, set the “Opacity” or the transform and click “◆ Set key”.
Repeat at another frame; the values blend automatically in between.
For a quick fade, click “Fade in” or “Fade out” from the current frame.
Under “Interpolation”, choose a linear or smooth curve.
“Point mix” blends the layer smoothly between splats and points, “Display” overrides the global mode.
sm.help.layerAnim.tips:
In the layer row of the timeline: double-click sets a key, drag moves it, right-click deletes it.
Opacity applies per splat: dense layers only fade visibly towards the end.
sm.help.layerAnim.title: Layer animation
sm.help.light.intro: Relights a scan: you dim the captured light and add up to four lights of your own, for example for a night scene.
sm.help.light.steps:
Open “Light” in the right toolbar and keep “Light on” switched on.
Lower “Scanned light” to darken the scene, and add base light with “Ambient” and “Ambient colour”.
Add a light with “+ Sun”, “+ Lamp” or “+ Spot”.
For the sun, set “Direction (°)” and “Height (°)”.
Place a lamp or spot with “Place” (click the model) or “At camera”; aim a spot at a point with “Aim”.
Adjust “Colour”, “Intensity”, “Range”, “Cone (°)” and “Softness”.
Use the key button in the panel header to set a key when the light should animate.
sm.help.light.tips:
New light brightens and tints, it cannot remove shadows that were captured.
Esc cancels placing.
The lights are not included in the player/VR export.
Lights also appear in the scene list under “Lights”: click one to move it with the arrows in the viewport, the cross or Delete removes it.
sm.help.light.title: Light
sm.help.look.intro: Gives the whole scene a film look with glow, grading, lens effects, fog and a colour LUT. The look applies in the viewport and in every export; the splat data is not changed.
sm.help.look.steps:
Open “Look” in the right toolbar and turn on “Look on”.
Under “Glow”, make bright areas glow with “Strength”, “Threshold”, “Radius” and “Glow colour”.
Under “Grading”, set “Exposure”, “Contrast”, “Saturation” and “Temperature”.
Under “Lens”, add “Vignette”, “Film grain” and “Chromatic aberration” if you like.
Hide ragged edges with “Fog”: “Strength”, “Start (m)” and “End (m)”.
Under “Colour LUT”, click “Load…” to pick a .cube file and adjust the “LUT strength”.
Use the ◇ key button in the panel header to set a key when the look should change over time.
sm.help.look.tips:
Vignette and chromatic aberration are not applied to 360° panoramas.
The player/VR export only approximates the look; grain, LUT and fog are missing there.
sm.help.look.title: Look
sm.help.pointCloud.intro: Sets how splats are drawn: as splats or as a point cloud, plus size and softness. This only affects display and rendering, not the splat data.
sm.help.pointCloud.steps:
Open “Display” in the properties of a splat.
Under “Mode”, choose “Splats” or “Point cloud”.
Adjust “Splat size” and “Softness”: smaller or lower looks crisper.
For the point cloud, set “Point size” and “Colour” (“Original” or “Uniform”).
Under “Advanced”, set “Size in” to “Pixels” or “World” and give the points some “Glow”.
sm.help.pointCloud.tips:
Single layers can override the mode under “Layer animation” → “Display”.
The mode also applies to the video export.
sm.help.pointCloud.title: Display
sm.help.quality.intro: Shows where a scan is blurry or weak and, with several scans, finds which one is sharper where. You can then select and delete the weak splats.
sm.help.quality.steps:
Open the quality tool in the right toolbar (U key).
Click “Compute scores”; under “Display”, the heatmap shows the weakest areas.
Set the “Threshold” and click “Select below threshold”.
With two or more visible scans, click “Compare scans” and adjust “Grid” and “Tolerance” if needed.
Click “Select worse” to pick splats that are sharper in another scan.
Delete the selection with Delete.
sm.help.quality.tips:
The heatmap is relative: it only shows the weakest areas of this one scan.
Compute the scores again after deleting.
The depth filter does not apply to “Select below threshold”.
sm.help.quality.title: Quality
sm.help.section.intro: Cuts the model from the top down, for example to remove the roof of a house down to the floor plan. Nothing is deleted, and the cut can be animated.
sm.help.section.steps:
Open the section tool in the right toolbar (Y key).
Drag the “Cut” slider: 0 % cuts nothing, 100 % cuts down to the floor plan height; or type the “Height (m)”.
If needed, use “Pick floor” and a click to set the floor height, and adjust the “Floor plan”.
Under “Applies to”, choose “All visible” or “Active layer”, and under “Edge”, “Soft” or “Hard”.
Turn on “Show plane” to see the cut height as a grid.
Use the key button next to the slider at different frames to animate the cut.
For an export without the roof, click “Select cut-off splats” and press Delete.
sm.help.section.tips:
“Re-measure” finds the top and bottom again, for example after deleting floaters.
The grid only shows in the editor, never in exports.
sm.help.section.title: Section
sm.help.titles.intro: Puts text over the image, for example a title, a place name or credits. It shows in the viewport and in image and video exports.
sm.help.titles.steps:
Open “Titles” in the right toolbar.
Move to the start frame on the timeline and click “+ Add title at current frame”.
Type the text and set the frame range with “Start at the current frame” and “End at the current frame”.
Set “Fade (s)” for fading in and out.
Choose “Position”, “Align”, “Size (%)”, “Font” and “Colour”, plus “Bold” and “Box” if needed.
“Show” jumps to the title, “Delete” removes it.
sm.help.titles.tips: Titles are not drawn into 360° exports.
sm.help.titles.title: Titles
sm.help.transitions.intro: Makes a layer appear or disappear with an effect, for example a glowing materialize from particles.
sm.help.transitions.steps:
Select a splat in the scene list and open “Transitions” in its properties.
Click “+ In” for a build-up or “+ Out” for a tear-down from the current frame; or Shift-drag (Shift+Alt-drag) in the layer row of the timeline.
Pick the effect: Sweep, Radial, Dissolve, Grow, Fly-in or Wave.
Set “Start / length”, “Easing”, “Direction” and “Origin”.
Fine-tune under “Advanced”, for example “Edge”, “Glow edge”, “Glow colour”, “Scatter” and “Swirl”.
Drag the block on the timeline or drag its ends; right-click or “Delete transition” removes it.
sm.help.transitions.tips:
For even phases in a dissolve, linear easing works best.
Before an in transition the layer is invisible, after an out transition it is gone.
Selection and picking always see the splats at their final position.
sm.help.transitions.title: Transitions
sm.image.depth-tip: Adds a Z channel with the camera distance per pixel (scene units, empty = 1e10). Colour is written in linear light.
sm.key.animated: Animated. Click to set a key at this frame
sm.key.changed: Changed but not keyed: the change is lost when the frame changes. Click to key it
sm.key.keyed: Key at this frame. Click to remove it
sm.key.static: Not animated. Click to set a key here and start animating this property
sm.light.add-from-list: Add a light in the light panel
sm.light.aim-tip: Click the model to aim the spot at that point.
sm.light.ambient-tip: Even light from all sides, e.g. a blue night sky after lowering the scanned light.
sm.light.azimuth-tip: Compass direction the sun shines from.
sm.light.baked-tip: How much of the light captured in the scan stays. 1 = as scanned, lower = darker (e.g. for night), then add your own lights.
sm.light.cone-tip: Half opening angle of the spot.
sm.light.elevation-tip: Height of the sun above the horizon. Low values give long grazing light.
sm.light.empty: Add up to four lights. The scan's own light stays baked into its colours: new light brightens and tints it, it cannot remove shadows that were captured.
sm.light.enabled-tip: Switches the added light off without losing it, to compare with the scan as captured.
sm.light.intensity-tip: Brightness of the light. Values above 4 can be typed in.
sm.light.picking: Click the model to place the light (Esc cancels).
sm.light.place-tip: Click the model to put the light just in front of that spot.
sm.light.props-hint: Drag the arrows in the viewport to move the light (the sun: its handle sets the direction). Delete removes it, Ctrl+Z undoes.
sm.light.range-tip: Distance (scene units) at which the light has faded out completely.
sm.light.title: Light
sm.light.to-camera-tip: Moves the light to the current view (a spot then shines where the camera looks).
sm.light.toggle-tip: Switch this light on or off
sm.light.wrap-tip: Lets the light wrap around surfaces. Higher values hide noisy surface directions of real scans.
sm.look.aberration-tip: Red and blue edges toward the corners, like a cheap lens. Not applied to 360° panoramas.
sm.look.bloom-tip: How strongly bright areas glow into their surroundings (bloom). 0 = off.
sm.look.contrast-tip: 1 = unchanged. Higher spreads darks and lights apart, lower flattens the image.
sm.look.enabled-tip: Switch the whole look on or off to compare. It applies in the viewport and in every image, video and 360° export; the splat data is not changed.
sm.look.exposure-tip: Brightness in stops: +1 doubles the light, −1 halves it.
sm.look.fog-color-tip: Off: far splats fade out into the background (also works with transparent exports). On: they take on the fog colour, like haze.
sm.look.fog-end-tip: Distance from the camera where the fog reaches full strength.
sm.look.fog-start-tip: Distance from the camera where the fog begins, in scene units (metres for most scans).
sm.look.fog-strength-tip: Distance fog: splats further away fade into the background (or into the fog colour). Great for hiding the ragged far edges of a scan. 0 = off.
sm.look.grain-tip: Fine noise like film grain; it changes every frame in videos. Also hides banding in soft gradients.
sm.look.lut-strength-tip: Blends between the image without (0) and with the LUT (1).
sm.look.lut-tip: Load a 3D LUT (.cube) from DaVinci Resolve, Premiere, Photoshop or a LUT pack to apply its colour look. It is saved with the project.
sm.look.radius-tip: How far the glow spreads: small = tight halo, large = wide haze.
sm.look.reset: Reset the look (keeps it switched on)
sm.look.saturation-tip: 1 = unchanged, 0 = black and white, 2 = very colourful.
sm.look.softness-tip: How gradually the vignette fades in from the centre.
sm.look.threshold-tip: Only areas brighter than this glow. Lower values let more of the scene glow (dreamy, soft); higher values keep the glow to highlights.
sm.look.tint-tip: Tints the glow. White keeps the colours of the glowing areas.
sm.look.title: Look
sm.look.vignette-tip: Darkens the corners of the frame. Not applied to 360° panoramas (they have no frame).
sm.motion-blur.shutter-tip: Share of the frame time the shutter is open: 0.5 is the classic 180° film shutter, 1 blurs the most.
sm.motion-blur.tip: Renders several in-between images per frame and averages them, so fast camera moves and animations blur like on a real camera. Takes as many times longer as there are sub-frames.
sm.motion-blur.title: Motion blur
sm.objects.title: Scene
sm.pano-preview.label: 360° preview · {{camera}} (equirectangular, as exported)
sm.pano-preview.label-stereo: 360° VR preview · {{camera}} (one eye, mono; the export is top/bottom stereo)
sm.pano.north-tip: Off: the panorama centre follows the camera's (or key's) view direction. On: the centre always faces world -Z
sm.pano.source-tip: Where the panorama comes from. For several panoramas you pick a folder
sm.path.handle-tip: Bezier handle: drag to shape the path (Alt moves it on its own), double-click returns to the automatic curve
sm.path.handles-hint: Handles: drag to shape the curve · Alt = break · double-click = auto
sm.path.hint: Drag a key or use the gizmo · Alt = position + target · Shift-click the path = insert key · Delete = remove · F = focus
sm.points.mode-tip: Global render mode, also applies to the video export
sm.points.size-in-tip: Pixels: constant on screen. World: gets smaller with distance
sm.points.size-tip: Point diameter in pixels or world units
sm.points.title: Point cloud
sm.properties.empty: Select a splat or a camera in the scene list to see its properties.
sm.properties.title: Properties
sm.quality.compare-scans-tip: Find the sharpest layer per voxel and mark worse splats
sm.quality.compute-tip: Compute the quality score for all visible layers
sm.quality.display-tip: The heatmap is relative: it shows the weakest areas of this scan. Whether one scan is sharper than another in a spot is shown by the comparison.
sm.quality.grid-tip: Comparison grid (voxel size, world units); 0 = automatic from the splat density
sm.quality.heatmap-hint: The heatmap is relative (weakest areas of this scan). Which scan is sharper where: "Compare scans".
sm.quality.need-two: The comparison needs at least two visible layers.
sm.quality.no-compare: The active layer has no comparison yet.
sm.quality.no-core: The score core is not connected yet.
sm.quality.no-scores: The active layer has no scores yet.
sm.quality.select-below-tip: Select splats of the active layer below the threshold (then press Delete)
sm.quality.select-worse-tip: Select splats of the active layer that are sharper in another scan
sm.quality.title: Quality
sm.quality.tolerance-tip: How much worse a layer has to be to get marked
sm.render.no-keys: The selected camera has no keys.
sm.section.axis-tip: World Y or the active layer's up axis (follows the orient tool)
sm.section.cut-tip: 0 % = nothing cut off, 100 % = down to the floor plan height above the floor
sm.section.edge-tip: Soft: the last centimetres fade out; hard: crisp cut
sm.section.floor-plan-tip: How much of the walls remains at 100 % (above the floor)
sm.section.height-tip: Absolute cut height along the axis, linked to the slider
sm.section.key-tip: Store the cut value at the current frame as a key
sm.section.measure-tip: Determine the top and bottom again from the visible splats
sm.section.pick-floor-tip: The next click in the viewport sets the floor height
sm.section.select-cut-tip: Select the cut-off splats of the active layer (then press Delete)
sm.section.show-plane-tip: Cut plane as a grid (editor only)
sm.section.title: Section
sm.splats.title: Splats
sm.stereo.ipd-tip: IPD in scene units: 0.064 = 6.4 cm in a scene in metres. Unscaled PLYs may use other units; adjust then (larger = stronger 3D effect)
sm.stereo.pole-tip: From this elevation (degrees above/below the horizon) the stereo fades softly into the mono panorama, so there are no double images at the top and bottom
sm.stereo.quality-tip: Number of azimuth strips per eye: more = cleaner disparity, longer render time
sm.stereo.quality-tip-video: Azimuth strips per eye: more = cleaner disparity, longer render time (6 + 2 × segments render passes per frame)
sm.timeline.auto-key-tip: Auto key: every property you change is keyed at the current frame right away (cameras, splats, section)
sm.timeline.cut-here-tip: Cut to this camera at the playhead
sm.timeline.cut-tip: Cut track: click a shot = go there, drag a shot's edge = shorten / lengthen it (the cut point moves), right-click = switch camera or delete. Drag in an empty area = new shot of the selected camera
sm.timeline.key-tip: The key button keys the listed properties of the selected camera or splat, plus every changed, not yet keyed value
sm.timeline.layer-tip: double-click = set key, drag a key = move, right-click a key = delete
sm.timeline.light-tip: Light track: click = key target; drag a key = move, right-click = delete
sm.timeline.live-tip: Shown by the cut at the playhead
sm.timeline.look-tip: Look track: click = key target; drag a key = move, right-click = delete
sm.timeline.section-tip: Section track: click = key target; drag a key = move, right-click = delete
sm.timeline.shot-tip: Drag the edges to trim, right-click to switch camera or delete
sm.timeline.transition-tip: {{kind}} transition {{effect}}: frame {{start}}–{{end}} (drag = move, ends = length, right-click = delete)
sm.titles.empty: Text over the image for a frame range, e.g. a title, a place name or credits. Shown in the viewport and drawn into image and video exports (not 360°).
sm.titles.title: Titles
sm.transform.xgrids-tip: Set the transform for XGrids scans (Z-up): position 0 0 0, rotation -90 0 0, scale 1
sm.transitions.add-in-tip: Build-up transition from the current frame (Shift+drag in the layer row works too)
sm.transitions.add-out-tip: Tear-down transition from the current frame (Shift+Alt+drag in the layer row)
sm.transitions.direction-tip: Axis for sweep and wave and for the swirl of fly-in. -Y with wave: rises from below
sm.transitions.drift-tip: Where the particles come from: outward from the origin, along the direction (e.g. +Y = from above) or random
sm.transitions.glow-tip: Strength of the glowing edge at the front
sm.transitions.noise-amount-tip: With axis/radial: how strongly the noise frays the front
sm.transitions.noise-freq-tip: Fineness of the noisy edge, relative to the layer size
sm.transitions.point-size-tip: Diameter of the glowing points in pixels
sm.transitions.scatter-tip: Flight or fall distance relative to the layer size
sm.transitions.threshold-tip: What drives the dissolve front: pure noise, a direction (axis) or radial from the origin, each with a noise share
sm.transitions.title: Transitions
sm.video.alpha-tip: Keeps the background transparent (alpha channel) for compositing and social videos
sm.video.depth-tip: Adds a Z channel with the camera distance per pixel (scene units, empty = 1e10) to every EXR frame
sm.video.format-tip: MOV + PNG codec: lossless with alpha, for Premiere, After Effects, Resolve and Final Cut. WebM: alpha for the web. PNG / EXR sequence: one image per frame into a folder; EXR in linear light with an optional depth channel (Z) for compositing.
sm.viewport.tip: The view the viewport shows: free, through a camera or the cut. Click to switch.
startup.failed: Splatmania failed to start. See the browser console for details.
startup.webgpu-unavailable: Splatmania requires WebGPU, which this browser does not support. Please try the latest Chrome, Edge or Safari.
tooltip.right-toolbar.quality: Quality: heatmap, threshold and scan comparison
tooltip.right-toolbar.section: Section: cut the model from the top down
tooltip.splat-data.log-bins: Space property-value bins logarithmically so groups across large ranges remain distinguishable.
tooltip.splat-data.log-counts: Scale histogram bin counts logarithmically so small counts remain visible alongside large ones.
tooltip.splat-data.on-screen-only: Only count splats visible in the camera's view. Off-screen splats are excluded from the histogram.
tooltip.splat-data.show-all: Show all per-splat properties in the list, including raw DC and spherical harmonic coefficients.
tooltip.timeline.key: Drag to move. Shift+drag to copy. Ctrl+click to set to current view.
tooltip.timeline.key-out-of-range: Keyframe {{frame}} is past the end of the timeline and won't play. Drag it onto the timeline or increase Total Frames.
